newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Evening Standard - April 4.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

An exclusive London-wide poll for the Evening Standard shows great discontent among voters for Tory plans to privatise the underground and policy pledges over health, education and housing. The anger threatens to spill over into a Labour landslide on 1 May.

- TAX RATES HIGHLIGHT DISUNITY IN EUROPE Research due to be published next week shows a wide disparity between the British system and its tax rates and those of its neighbours on the Continent. Harmonisation of tax systems in Europe is looking more unlikely than achieving European monetary union in the short term.

-- THAILAND EASES PROPERTY RESTRICTIONS Thailand is set to relax current restrictions on foreign ownership of real estate. The move will help boost dropping property values threatening to drag some financial institutions into bankruptcy.

-- GREENBACK RALLIES Ahead of today's key US employment figures, the US dollar nervously recovered lost ground yesterday. An overnight meeting between US Treasury Secretary Robin Rubin and Japanese Prime Minister Hashimoto ended with signals that no moves will be made to adjust currency values.

-- NEW BREED OF NON-EXECS TAKE ON WATCHDOG ROLE Sir Adrian Cadbury's report on corporate governance five years ago, saw the advent of a new breed of younger, more committed non-executive directors. Serving chief execs of public companies who are now headhunted as opposed to recruited via the old boy network are much sought after as non-execs, responsibilities as corporate watchdogs and positions on audit committees.
-- EUROPE AND US IN CHINA AIR BATTLE Boeing and Airbus Industrie are battling for the world's fastest growing aviation market in China. Aircraft contracts are in great dispute.
